page: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation is constrained to 16.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes 472 GB of bundled local storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data shows strong performance in single-threaded tasks, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2166.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.52 GB/sec. Text processing is also strong at 2689.0. Multi-core and memory-bound workloads generally register in the average tier, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 8360.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 14260.83. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is measured at 67.27 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the hardware supports Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), enabling strong text generation speeds of 313.4 tokens/sec on small 135M LLM models, though text generation performance drops to a weak 7.97 tokens/sec on medium 7B models.

The D8lds_v6 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints, due to its low memory-to-vCPU ratio. However, the 16.0 GB memory limit represents a significant tradeoff, restricting its utility for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. This server is suited for CPU-bound tasks such as software compilation, web serving, text processing, and lightweight machine learning inference on small models.
